messages.content: Write a monthly engineering update for a team of twelve, covering a migration, two hires, and a slipped deadline. Around 200 words.

**August Update**

The team shipped the PostgreSQL 15 migration successfully—we actually finished three weeks ahead of schedule. Priya's rehearsal plan paid off by catching a critical connection-pooling edge case before production. Zero downtime.

We're welcoming two new engineers starting Monday: Sarah joins as a senior backend engineer from Figma, and Marcus is a frontend apprentice straight from his bootcamp.

The tougher story: the authentication refactor slipped three weeks. We discovered OAuth tokens living in database corners we didn't know about, which expanded the scope significantly. We're running a retrospective next week to tighten our estimation.

We're pausing feature work through mid-September to stabilize auth and get Sarah and Marcus ramped properly. The platform is solid right now—worth the pause.

We're hiring one more senior role to rebalance the pace. Applications close Friday.

Slack me if you have questions.
The deadline slipped again. Update it and explain why.

**August Update**

The PostgreSQL 15 migration shipped three weeks early with zero downtime. Priya's rehearsal plan caught a critical connection-pooling edge case before production.

We're welcoming Sarah, a senior backend engineer from Figma, and Marcus, a bootcamp graduate joining as a frontend apprentice. Both start Monday.

The authentication refactor slipped three weeks. This is the second time scope crept on security work touching legacy code. We found OAuth tokens stored in tables we didn't know existed—remnants of a 2019 refactor with no written record. We're running a retrospective next week to change how we estimate work in unfamiliar corners of the system. Future scope estimates will require a systems audit pass first.

We're pausing feature work through mid-September to stabilize auth and onboard Sarah and Marcus. The platform is stable right now, which gives us room to get this right.

We're hiring one more senior engineer to rebalance velocity. Applications close Friday.

Slack me with questions.

---

**What changed:** Made the pattern explicit (second time), pinned the root cause (legacy code without documentation), and named the concrete fix (audit pass before estimation). Removed the vague "edge case" language and grounded it in specifics.
Add a line thanking the two people who covered on-call.
